chunks.heading: Purpose
chunks.text: The Saaya Relief Programme (fictional) gives a quarterly cash transfer of Rs 12,000 to widows in financial need. This is a prototype policy written for a hackathon; it is not an official document.

chunks.heading: No fees
chunks.text: The programme never charges any fee for registration, processing or payment. Anyone asking for money to release a payment is committing fraud.

chunks.heading: Official messages
chunks.text: Official messages come only from the sender IDs SAAYA and 7240. Official messages never contain links and never ask for a PIN, a code or a photo of a CNIC.

chunks.heading: Who may apply
chunks.text: The applicant must be a woman whose identity is confirmed in the identity registry.

chunks.heading: Age
chunks.text: The applicant must be at least 18 years old on the date of the decision.

chunks.heading: Widowhood
chunks.text: The applicant's husband must be deceased, as shown by a death record in the civil registry or a signed death certificate.

chunks.heading: Time since death
chunks.text: The husband's death must have occurred within the ten years before the application.

chunks.heading: Remarriage
chunks.text: An applicant who has remarried after her husband's death is not eligible.

chunks.heading: Household income
chunks.text: The household income must not exceed Rs 40,000 per month.

chunks.heading: Residence
chunks.text: The applicant must live in a district served by the office where she applies.

chunks.heading: Identity card validity
chunks.text: An expired identity card is a warning for the officer and not a reason for rejection.

chunks.heading: Documents
chunks.text: A clear photo of the identity card and the death certificate is required. If a photo is unclear, the applicant is asked for one specific retake, at most twice.

chunks.heading: Decisions
chunks.text: Only an officer may reject an application. Every rejection states a reason code, and the applicant may complain.

chunks.heading: Payment
chunks.text: An approved payment is held for a short cooling-off period before it is sent, and the exact amount is confirmed to the applicant by voice.

chunks.heading: Payout changes
chunks.text: A change of payout wallet needs the applicant's PIN, an officer's approval, a cooling-off period and a notice to the old number.

chunks.heading: Helpers
chunks.text: A community helper may assist a family only while that family has unlocked its case. Helpers never collect money or PINs.

chunks.heading: Complaints
chunks.text: An applicant who received less than the full amount can file a complaint with one tap; the complaint is linked to the payment and to any helper.

chunks.heading: Consent
chunks.text: The applicant can see who holds her data, hear who opened it, and withdraw consent. Withdrawal pauses the case.

chunks.heading: Corrections
chunks.text: The applicant can ask for a wrong field to be corrected; an officer reviews the request and the old value is kept in history.
